propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Clementissime Deus, qui sanctum Silvestrum Abbatem, saeculi hujus
vanitatem in aperto tumulo pie meditantem, ad eremum vocare et praeclaris
vitae meritis decorare dignatus es: te supplices exoramus; ut, ejus exemplo
terrena despicientes, tui consortio perfruamur aeterno. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n1297, printed p. 1297, running head `NOV. 26-ST. SYLVESTER`, under `Prayer` in the Mass headed `St. Sylvester, Abbot`. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer, with differences only in pointing, capitalisation and the witness's abbreviated conclusion. This is an ordinary numbered page and not one of the excluded 1298a-1298n appendix leaves.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: O most merciful God, Who, when the holy abbot Sylvester was piously pondering over the vanity of earthly things whilst he stood by an open grave, didst vouchsafe to call him to the desert, we supplicate Thee that, despising earthly things, after his example, we may forever enjoy Thy presence. Through our Lord.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Quaesumus, Domine: ut, dum haec munera divinae majestati tuae reverenter
offerimus; pia mentis praeparatione et cordis puritate, beati Silvestri
Abbatis imitatores effecti, Corpus et Sanguinem Filii tui sancte percipere
mereamur: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n1298, printed p. 1298, under `Secret` in the Mass of St Sylvester. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer, with differences only in pointing, capitalisation and the witness's abbreviation of the conclusion to `Qui tecum`. Printed p. 1298 is the ordinary numbered page immediately before, and is not part of, the excluded 1298a-1298n appendix.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: We beseech Thee, O Lord, that, while we reverently offer these gifts to Thy divine majesty we may by pious preparation of soul and purity of heart, following the example of blessed abbot Sylvester, become worthy to partake holily of the body and blood of Thy Son. Who with Thee.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Divina dape refectis tribue, quaesumus, Domine: sancti Silvestri Abbatis
vestigiis ita inhaerere; ut copiosam mercedem in regno gloriae tuae cum
Sanctis habeamus. Per Dominum nostrum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n1298, printed p. 1298, under `Postcommunion` in the Mass of St Sylvester. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer, with differences only in pointing and capitalisation. Printed p. 1298 is outside the excluded lettered appendix.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: We pray Thee, O Lord, that Thou grant unto us, refreshed with the divine banquet, to follow closely the footsteps of the holy abbot Sylvester, that we may have an abundant reward with the saints in the kingdom of Thy glory. Through our Lord.
